notes: The San Francisco City Planning Commission's minutes of its regular and special meetings, January to December 1972, from the four quarterly volumes the San Francisco Public Library contributed to the Internet Archive (20-23minutesofsanfran1972sa). Pages were split from the hOCR search text on the Internet Archive page index, counting the viewer page among the leaves scandata.xml does not mark addToAccessFormats=false (checked against the scan of 20minutesofsanfran1972sa n10, page 4 of the 6 January 1972 minutes). Every page is dated from the meeting header it sits under. Four kinds of finding: what the Commission decided about a property, dated to the meeting that decided it; what the minutes state stood on or occupied the property; dated past facts the minutes state about a building; and landmark designations. A proposal on its own is not a finding. A Board of Supervisors or committee action the minutes report without its own date is framed 'by' the date of the meeting that reported it. The minutes name applicants, owners, attorneys, objectors, commissioners and staff throughout; the reader spec barred all of them from every field, and kept companies, institutions, named buildings and architects.

coverage.remaining: Every page of the four 1972 volumes (20minutesofsanfran1972sa, 21minutesofsanfran1972sa, 22minutesofsanfran1972sa, 23minutesofsanfran1972sa) was read. Volumes 24-39 (1973-1980) and 40-58 (1994-2005) remain. Of the 251 unresolved, 196 print no street number: they are located only by a corner, a bearing, a block, or a building name with no page to carry it (the year's height-and-bulk hearings, the Stockton-Sacramento and Nihonmachi redevelopment cases, street vacations, surplus-lot sales, Playland, the Russian Hill tower sites at Green and Jones and at Hyde and Lombard); 29 are condominium parcels today (1150 Lombard, 301 Castro, 1800 Fillmore, 3900 California, 1130 Sacramento, and five Russian Hill apartment towers whose number EAS still files on the building's original lot), waiting on #446; 21 have no EAS record at the number (119 Broadway, 1863 Greenwich, 1999 Market, 4277 Mission, 608 Commercial apart from the Mint's own page); the rest are ranges now split across parcels. Named buildings were placed by hand where the site already has the page (24 findings); speakers' height-hearing remarks about named towers and hospitals were left unresolved.
coverage.note: 1,006 OCR pages with text out of 1,942 scanned leaves, read by ten parallel readers from one written spec; 43 meetings dated; 382 findings: 174 statements of what stood on a property, 128 decisions, 65 dated past facts, 15 landmark designations. Every quote was re-anchored mechanically against its own page before the file was written (382 of 382 anchored). 131 resolved: 107 by the EAS join on a printed number, 24 by hand on a building the site already carries (the House of the Flag, the Original U.S. Mint, the Sherman House, the Geary-Presidio car barn, Pacific Medical Center, Davies Medical Center, the National Guard Armory, the Hall of Justice, the Levi Strauss factory, the Conservatory of Flowers). Five EAS joins on Russian Hill apartment towers were taken back to unresolved: the parcel has no roll row because the building is a condominium on C-series unit lots. 101 published on 53 pages (20 of them seeded, 1 a place page) as 67 timeline entries; 30 declined: 18 already on the page from another source or an earlier volume, 7 repeats within the batch, 3 meeting venues, 1 statement about four lots now several parcels, and 1 billboard behind a building. The 1860-against-1864 date of the House of the Flag was already a stated conflict on its page.
